baseline_accuracy.reading: the baseline's total-points error is only marginally better than guessing the league-average total: it is a descriptive matchup summary, not a sharp scorer. Treat its point estimates as loosely informative and widen every range accordingly

how_to_use: p_*_greater_than tables give P(outcome > threshold) among past games whose pre-kickoff baseline resembled this one. They show spread and skew, including how often a favourite fails a spread. They are NOT calibrated probabilities for this game: shift them for the matchup, QB, injuries and weather evidence, and widen your range when the reference class is thin.
